questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify the original source in a chain

stimulus.body: The brief cites a handbook that summarises a code that quotes a test report.

questions.stem: Which document is the primary source in this chain?

options.text: The code, because it is official.
The handbook, because it is most recent.
The test report, because it contains the original observation.
All three are primary because they are published.

questions.explanation: The test report holds the original observation. Handbook and code are intermediaries, and publication does not make a source primary.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Rewrite an unattributed claim with a source
questions.stem: Rewrite the unattributed claim the new joint is strongest into a properly attributed claim for a brief.

answer.exemplar: Attribute it to a named test, for example Jones 2024 tensile tests on the joint under BS EN 1993, reporting a 20 percent higher capacity than the previous design.

questions.explanation: An attributed claim names the tester, method and comparison. An unattributed claim cannot be verified or located.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify vague attribution in a stimulus

stimulus.body: According to recent findings, the new drainage scheme outperforms all older alternatives.

questions.stem: What is the main weakness of this attribution?

options.text: Outperforms is a precise enough measure.
Recent is acceptable because it signals currency.
options.misconception: treats a time word as sourcing

options.text: The claim is fine if the scheme is patented.
Recent findings names no author, title or year to locate the source.

questions.explanation: Recent findings identifies no source. Currency words, patents or precise wording do not enable verification.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a bare statistic needs a denominator
questions.stem: Why does a bare percentage need its denominator?

options.text: Denominators are only needed in medical studies.
options.misconception: limits a general requirement to one field

options.text: The denominator shows the size of the group the percentage describes.
Percentages are self-explanatory without denominators.
The denominator can be guessed from context.

questions.explanation: A percentage describes a share of a group, so the group size must be stated. Field limits, self-explanation or guessing do not suffice.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify a missing title in a citation
questions.stem: A brief cites Author X, 2018, Journal of Materials, pp 10-20, but no title. Why is this incomplete?

options.text: Page numbers alone identify the paper.
The journal name is enough to find any paper.
Without the title the reader cannot identify which paper is meant.
The author's surname is sufficient.
options.misconception: ignores that authors publish many papers

questions.explanation: A title identifies the paper. Journal, pages or surname alone may match many papers by the same author.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Explain why repeated measurement beats single snapshot
questions.stem: Why does repeated measurement strengthen a claim about a design change?

answer.exemplar: Repeated measurements reveal trends and variability, making it easier to separate a real change from random fluctuation or a one-off event.

questions.explanation: Single snapshots can be noise. Repeated measures show pattern and variability, supporting stronger claims.
questions.hint: One point could be an outlier.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Choose the more reliable source for a safety claim

stimulus.body: The brief chooses between a manufacturer brochure and the original test report for a load rating.

questions.stem: Which source is more reliable for the load rating and why?

options.text: Neither is needed if the product is certified.
options.misconception: relies on certification instead of data

options.text: The brochure, because the manufacturer knows the product best.
Both are equally reliable for engineering decisions.
The test report, because it documents method and data.

questions.explanation: A test report documents method and data. A brochure is marketing, and certification alone does not replace documented testing.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Spot an unattributed causal claim
questions.stem: The brief states the new bracing eliminated all vibration problems.

options.text: Eliminated is acceptable if the bracing is patented.
The claim is unattributed and absolute, with no test or scope named.
The claim is fine because vibration is easy to measure.
All vibration problems is a reasonable summary.

questions.explanation: An absolute claim with no test or scope cannot be verified. Patent, measurability or summary do not support it.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Explain why vague attribution blocks verification
questions.stem: Why does vague attribution such as a recent study prevent verification?

answer.exemplar: A recent study names no author, title or year, so a reader cannot locate, read or check the original work to confirm the claim.

questions.explanation: Vague labels identify no source. Without author, title or year, verification is impossible.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify a statistic missing a definition

stimulus.body: The brief reports a 50 percent improvement in reliability.

questions.stem: What definition is missing from this 50 percent claim?

options.text: The colour of the reliability dashboard.
The brand of the reliability software used.
How reliability was defined and measured.
The names of the reliability engineers.

questions.explanation: A percentage needs the measure defined. Software brand, dashboard colour or engineer names do not define reliability.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Verify a citation has all core components

stimulus.body: The brief cites Chen, Durability of recycled aggregate concrete, 2022, Construction and Building Materials, 314, 125678.

questions.stem: Is this citation complete enough to retrieve the paper?

options.text: No, it lacks the paper's word count.
No, it lacks the author's institution.
options.misconception: adds an optional element as required

options.text: No, it lacks the number of references.
Yes, it has author, title, year, journal and article number.

questions.explanation: Author, title, year, journal and article number suffice for retrieval. Institution, reference count or word count are not core components.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a trend beats a single comparison
questions.stem: Why is a trend line stronger than a single before and after comparison?

options.text: A single comparison is always more accurate.
It shows direction and variability across multiple points.
Trend lines are only for financial data.
options.misconception: limits a general method to one domain

options.text: Trends ignore all measurement error.

questions.explanation: A trend reveals direction and variability across points. Single comparisons can be noise, and trends do not eliminate all error.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Explain when secondary evidence is acceptable
questions.stem: When is secondary evidence acceptable in a design brief?

answer.exemplar: Secondary evidence is acceptable for background context or low-stakes claims, but primary evidence is needed for safety-critical or novel claims.

questions.explanation: Secondary sources suit background and low-stakes uses. Critical claims need primary evidence to avoid inherited distortion.
questions.hint: How much hinges on the claim?

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify an unattributed recommendation

stimulus.body: Best practice dictates that the new joint should be used in all seismic zones.

questions.stem: Why is best practice a weak basis here?

options.text: The claim is fine if the joint is certified.
Best practice is always correct in engineering.
It names no source, standard or scope for the practice.
Seismic zones are well understood, so sourcing is unnecessary.

questions.explanation: Best practice names no source or scope. Authority labels, certification or familiarity do not substantiate it.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Rewrite a vague body into a specific source
questions.stem: Rewrite the vague phrase industry guidelines suggest into a specific attribution for a brief.

answer.exemplar: Name the guideline body, document title and edition, for example the Institution of Structural Engineers 2023 guidance on retrofit, section 5.1.

questions.explanation: Specific attribution names body, document and edition. A vague phrase cannot be located or verified.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify a statistic missing uncertainty
questions.stem: The brief gives a single efficiency value with no range or confidence. What is missing?

options.text: The number of pages in the report.
The name of the efficiency tester.
The colour of the test equipment.
The uncertainty or confidence interval around the value.

questions.explanation: A single value without uncertainty overstates precision. Tester name, equipment colour or page count do not address precision.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a citation needs a retrieval path
questions.stem: Why does a citation need a retrieval path such as a DOI or URL?

answer.exemplar: A retrieval path lets a reader locate and open the exact source, so the claim can be verified rather than taken on trust.

questions.explanation: Without a retrieval path, a citation cannot be checked. A DOI or URL enables direct access to the source.
